Here is a draft ADR:

# ADR-0007: Use PostgreSQL for the orders service

Status: Proposed

## Context
The orders service needs transactional writes and flexible reporting queries. The team already operates PostgreSQL for billing.

## Decision
We will use PostgreSQL 16 as the primary datastore for the orders service.

## Consequences
- We reuse the existing backup and monitoring tooling.
- Reporting queries can use SQL directly.
- We accept vertical scaling limits for write throughput.

Is the Context section enough?

It is enough to follow the decision, but it does not name the alternatives that were considered. A sentence on why a document store or a managed service was rejected would make the record more useful.
Change the status to Accepted and add a line "Date: 2026-10-06" right under it.

The top of the file now reads:

Status: Accepted
Date: 2026-10-06

The rest is unchanged.
Add a consequence: we must plan a partitioning strategy before we reach 50M orders.

Added as the last bullet under ## Consequences:

- We must plan a partitioning strategy before we reach 50M orders.

The rest is unchanged.
Give me the final ADR as a complete file I can commit.

required_facts: The status is Accepted and the line "Date: 2026-10-06" follows it
The Context section is complete: transactional writes and flexible reporting queries, and the team already operates PostgreSQL for billing
The Decision says PostgreSQL 16 is the primary datastore for the orders service
Consequences has all four bullets: reuse backup and monitoring tooling, reporting queries in SQL, vertical scaling limits for write throughput, and planning a partitioning strategy before 50M orders
The text is complete, with no placeholders or elision markers
critical_omissions: Using "...", "unchanged" or similar placeholders in place of any section
Missing the status change, the date, or the partitioning consequence
unnecessary_repetition: Re-explaining the earlier feedback on alternatives
Commentary on each edit beyond a one-line note
